result_text:
GATE 3 DECISION BRIEF — items 1-5. Repo @ main, read-only, no edits made. Facts only; no recommendations, per hard constraints. METHOD NOTE: `research/results/DISCREPANCY_LEDGER.md` (prior task_2026-09-04_001) already independently covers items 1, 2, part of 3, and flags item 4 as an open bonus question. This pass re-verified those claims firsthand against live code/files (not just cited the ledger) and found net-new deltas in items 3 and 4 — flagged inline below. ═══ ITEM 1 — WP3 PDF-export claim + WP5 CLI flag claim ═══ cli.py::build_parser() (full 195-line file read): single flat argparse.ArgumentParser, no add_subparsers() anywhere. Complete flag set (10 total): --predictions-file/-i, --true-label-col, --predicted-label-col, --race-col, --gender-col, --age-col, --protected-attr/-a, --output-report/-o, --model-name, --dataset-name, --explain. No `audit` subcommand. No --backend. No --bca-bootstrap. Claim source: dev-logs/weekly-reports/2026-08-27_WK4_report.md:39 — "`bias-aperture audit` CLI with `--explain`, `--backend`, and `--bca-bootstrap` flags" | Completed. Only --explain exists. WP3 PDF claim source: README.md:60 — report module "renders...HTML/PDF compliance reports." Verified: zero PDF-related imports in src/bias_aperture/report/*.py (checked weasyprint/pdfkit/wkhtmltopdf/xhtml2pdf), zero PDF dependency in pyproject.toml. HTML-only in practice. Corroboration: DISCREPANCY_LEDGER.md Section D independently reached both conclusions ("WP3's PDF-export claim is entirely unsupported"; CLI flags "does not match actual cli.py") — this pass confirms via direct cli.py/pyproject.toml read rather than citing the ledger alone. Rough effort — add vs. correct: | Sub-claim | Current state | Effort to ADD | Effort to CORRECT claim only | |---|---|---|---| | `audit` subcommand | Flat parser, no subparsers | Moderate: restructure build_parser() to add_subparsers(), move all 10 flags under `audit`, update main()'s arg access, update the 2 existing CLI tests (per ledger Section D) that invoke the current flat form | Trivial: reword one dev-log line | | `--backend` (single-backend select) | CrossValidationOrchestrator.run(records, protected_attr) [backends.py:984] has no backend param — always runs both | Non-trivial + touches a locked invariant: CONTEXT.md's "Dual-Backend Architecture" states Fairlearn+AIF360 cross-validation is by-design. Adding single-backend mode needs a scope decision first, then new branching in run() + CLI plumbing | Trivial | | `--bca-bootstrap` (override resample count) | statistics.py:136 — bootstrap fn already takes `n_resamples: int = MIN_BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES` as a parameter | Small-to-moderate: capability exists at function level; needs CLI arg → new param on run() (doesn't currently accept one either) → threaded to call site. No architectural conflict | Trivial | ═══ ITEM 2 — WP5 "90%" claim ═══ 10,954 / 97,698 = 11.21% (computed). Ground truth (docs/research/CLAIM_LEDGER.md R-002, cross-checked in 4 other docs): 97,698 = 86,744 train + 10,954 val, confirmed via line-count of official FairFace CSVs. So 10,954 IS the complete validation split, not a partial run. README.md:158 already frames the processed-image figure as `10,954/10,954` (against the val-split denominator = 100%), not against 97,698. The "90%" in README:158 and CONTEXT.md attaches to WP5 workstream/milestone completion (report review + main.pdf finalization outstanding) — not to image-processing coverage. On their face, "90% workstream" and "11.2% of full release" measure different things and aren't in direct conflict. Separate, more precise framing from DISCREPANCY_LEDGER.md Section D / "Key flags" #3: the project's own CLAIM_LEDGER.md tier system reserves "VALIDATED" for a full 97,698-image run; actual completed run is val-split-only. So no claim can reach "VALIDATED" tier yet regardless of how "90%" is read — that's a ledger-tier gap distinct from the raw-percentage question. ═══ ITEM 3 — architecture_highlevel.jpg stale elements ═══ Image directly viewed (not just cross-referenced from text). Full stale-element list, with cluster attribution: Per ledger Cluster C directly (2 items): 1. "Orchestration & configuration layer: CLI + YAML config" box — verified stale: zero yaml dependency in pyproject.toml, zero `import yaml` anywhere in src/. cli.py is pure argparse. 2. UTKFace box: "20,000+ images," solid arrow, equal visual weight to FairFace — verified stale against README's own Mermaid (README.md lines 18-53): `UTK[("UTKFace dataset
[CUT] profiled only")]` with dashed `classDef cut stroke-dasharray: 5 5`, connected only to a "Research comparison" node. Image contradicts the repo's own already-correct diagram. Filed under Cluster B, not C — same image (1 item; flagging since the task scoped to "cluster C" specifically): 3. "Explainability layer: SHAP" box, no caveat. Actual behavior: SHAP attempted, falls back to explain_surrogate() (demographic-dummy linear Shapley) per explainability.py / README:12's own correct caveat elsewhere. NOT filed under any cluster in the existing ledger — found via direct image inspection this pass (2 items): 4. "FairFace dataset — 108,501 images" box. Stale per Cluster A / CLAIM_LEDGER R-002 (released count is 97,698; 108,501 = pre-annotation-discard total). Cluster A's own stale-108,501 table (ledger lines 13-22) does NOT list this image among its hits (lists back.tex, main.pdf p.36, BiasAperture-AT.md, track files — not this image). Checked for overlap with the "main.pdf p.36" row: this image is \includegraphics'd at systemArchitectureAndMethodology.tex:18 (early in that chapter); the p.36 hit is backmatter text (NFR-004 table, necessarily later in the compiled PDF) — different page, different instance. Appears to be a genuinely uncounted occurrence. 5. "Compliance report (HTML/PDF)" box at diagram bottom. Stale per same evidence as Item 1 (zero PDF code/dependency). Not tied to this specific image anywhere in the existing ledger (Section D discusses the PDF claim re: README/WP3 generally, not this diagram). Net: Cluster C's own table names 2 stale elements in this image. Full count across all evidence (this pass + Cluster B) is 5. ═══ ITEM 4 — report/generator.py vs report/templates/generator.py ═══ Path note: no generator.py exists anywhere under the top-level report/ (LaTeX proposal) directory (contains only main.tex/main.pdf/src/{chapters,images,frontmatter,backmatter}). Read as src/bias_aperture/report/generator.py vs src/bias_aperture/report/templates/generator.py. Diff: byte-identical except one trailing-newline difference at EOF (223 vs 224 lines, newline-only). Import resolution: - src/bias_aperture/report/__init__.py imports from `bias_aperture.report.generator` (top-level file), re-exports HTMLReportGenerator/ReportContext/REGULATORY_MAPPING. - cli.py:20 imports HTMLReportGenerator, ReportContext from `bias_aperture.report` → resolves to the top-level generator.py. - src/tests/test_report_generator.py:9 imports directly from `bias_aperture.report.generator` — same top-level file. - src/bias_aperture/report/templates/generator.py: zero references anywhere. Ran the task's exact specified grep (`grep -rn 'import.*generator' src/ report/`, case-sensitive) — zero hits total, including for the LIVE file, because actual imports use `HTMLReportGenerator` (capital G), not lowercase substring "generator". This is a case-sensitivity artifact of that exact pattern, not evidence either file is unused. Re-ran case-insensitively (`grep -rni`) — confirms live file is imported 2 places, templates/ copy is imported nowhere. templates/ also has no __init__.py, so it isn't set up as an importable subpackage at all. - templates/'s actual role: holds report.html.j2, the Jinja2 template the live generator.py loads (`FileSystemLoader(self.template_dir)`, `get_template("report.html.j2")` — generator.py lines 57-62, 201). The stray generator.py copy is unrelated to that role. Verdict: src/bias_aperture/report/templates/generator.py is dead code. src/bias_aperture/report/generator.py is live. Cross-reference: DISCREPANCY_LEDGER.md Section C flagged the duplication as "Bonus (out of scope)... near-duplicate/dead-code files defining the same classes twice. Not doc-claimed, not scored" but did not resolve which copy is dead. This pass resolves that open question. ═══ ITEM 5 — fellowship PDFs: source-file check + §13 precedent ═══ Source search (repo-wide, this pass): - docs/fellowship/ has 5 PDFs; only BiasAperture_User_Requirement_Document.pdf and BiasAperture_Literature_Review.pdf are in question (other 3 are fellowship-provided templates/reference material, not BiasAperture deliverables). - No .tex/.md source anywhere for either file (consistent with prior pass). - No .docx or .odt file anywhere in the repo (`find . -iname "*.docx" -o -iname "*.odt"` — zero hits). - No docs/fellowship/src/ or similarly-named staging/draft dir — docs/ has exactly 3 subdirs total: research/, research/pdf/, fellowship/. - No Google Docs/LibreOffice/OpenOffice signatures in either PDF's raw byte stream (`strings | grep -i "google|libreoffice|openoffice|writer"` — zero hits, both files). New this pass: `pdfinfo` on both shows Creator/Producer = "Microsoft® Word for Microsoft 365" for both (URD created 2026-08-13; Lit Review created 2026-08-18). A .docx source almost certainly existed at authoring time — it was simply never committed to this repo (may still exist locally/in the author's Microsoft 365 account). This is a different conclusion than "no source ever existed": it's "no source is trackable in-repo," confirmed more precisely than the prior pass. §13 precedent (docs/BiasAperture-AT.md, "Outstanding Action Items" — two duplicate copies of this file exist in-repo, docs/ and "research/context feed/", already flagged elsewhere under Cluster A as unrelated duplication; used the docs/ copy): Concerns feasibility_study.pdf — another already-submitted, PDF-only artifact with no live in-repo source — which had two known content gaps (missing Aequitas citation §2.2; missing SHAP module-list entry §3.1.3). Resolution pattern actually followed (per the log's revision history, v3→v5, July 30–Aug 7 2026, still open as of latest entry): 1. Both gaps logged as explicit "Outstanding Action Item" table rows (Item/Description/Target/Status) rather than the PDF being hand-edited or reconstructed. 2. When the same content need (SHAP module) arose in a document WITH a live compilable source (report/src/chapters/requirements.tex), the fix was applied there instead (FR-005 added) — log explicitly notes this resolves the requirement in one document while feasibility_study.pdf itself remains separately, explicitly outstanding: "Two different documents; feasibility_study.pdf edit itself remains outstanding." 3. The PDF itself was never directly patched across 3+ tracked revisions — the gap is carried forward as a known, transparent, unresolved item rather than force-closed. Reported as-found per the task's ask; no application of this pattern proposed for the two new PDFs. ITEM 6: skipped per spec (Aaradhya sign-off item, no research needed).
